title: Spokane Window Rebates 2026: Avista Pays Up to $225 per Window
desc: Spokane window and sliding glass door rebates for 2026: Avista's $180 to $225 per window, $480 to $600 per sliding door, storm window rebates and the 120-day deadline.
h1: Window and Door Rebates in Spokane
badge: Up to $225 per window from Avista
lead: Avista pays up to $225 per window and up to $600 per sliding glass door for replacing existing ones with tighter models. You can also get a smaller rebate for installing the windows yourself.
cards_heading: What window rebates pay in Spokane
cards_intro: We read Avista's Washington window rebate page on October 6, 2026. The rebate depends on a window's U-factor, a number that shows how fast heat leaks through. A lower number means a tighter window. The home must be an existing single-family primary residence that heats with Avista electricity or natural gas.

cards.title: Windows installed by a contractor
cards.note: $180 for a U-factor of 0.29 to 0.23 and $225 for 0.22 or lower.

cards.title: Windows you install yourself
cards.note: Half the contractor amount. You must sign Avista's self-certification and send photos of the finished job.

cards.title: Sliding glass doors
cards.note: With a contractor. Self-installed doors earn $240 or $300.

cards.title: Storm windows
cards.note: With a contractor, for ENERGY STAR certified storm windows or ones with a low-emissivity coating. $4.00 for self-install.

cards.title: Federal tax credit
cards.note: The federal window credit ended with the other home energy credits for 2026 installs, per the IRS page on the clean energy credit.

after_cards:
Working it out

A Spokane family that replaces eight windows with units rated 0.22 or lower, using a contractor, gets 8 times $225, which is $1,800. If two of those are sliding glass doors at $600 each and six are windows at $225, the total is $1,200 plus $1,350, or $2,550. If the same family does the install itself, the total is $1,275 at most.
sections:
The US Census Bureau's American Community Survey (2020 to 2024) says about 68 percent of Spokane homes were built before 1980, and 26 percent before 1940. Older homes are more likely to have older windows, though replaced windows are common too. About 54 percent of homes use gas as their main heat and 42 percent use electricity, so Avista's window rebate reaches both fuel types.

Windows are usually the most expensive item on this list for the rebate they bring. A rebate of $225 on a window that costs several times more is a small share of the bill. The better reason to replace is comfort or damage, not the rebate alone.
How to read a window label

Every efficient window carries a sticker from the National Fenestration Rating Council with a U-factor. Avista wants that number for every window and sliding door on your final invoice. The two tiers are 0.29 to 0.23 and 0.22 or below. A seller may show a window rated 0.30, which falls just outside the rebate. Always check the number against these tiers before you order.

You must apply within 120 days of the installation, and bids and estimates are not accepted as proof. Include the final invoice that shows how many windows and doors were installed, the U-factor of each and the cost. You may apply online, by email to rebates@myavista.com, by fax or by mail. Seasonal and recreational homes are not eligible, and neither is new construction. The windows must replace existing ones.
claim_heading: How to claim Spokane window rebates
claim_steps: Check that Avista sends your electric or gas bill.
Choose windows with a U-factor of 0.29 or lower, and ask for the stickers or packing slips that show the number.
Pick a licensed contractor, or plan to self-install and sign the self-certification.
Keep the final invoice and the U-factor proof for every window.
faq: How much does Avista pay for windows?
$180 per window for a U-factor of 0.29 to 0.23, and $225 for 0.22 or lower, when a contractor installs them. Self-install pays half.
Do I need to use a contractor?
No. Avista pays half the amount for homeowner installs, with photos and a signed self-certification.
Is there a cap on how many windows?
The page we read did not state a cap. Ask Avista if you are replacing a whole house of windows.
Yes. Avista pays $480 or $600 per sliding glass door with a contractor and $240 or $300 for self-install.
No. The IRS says the federal clean energy credit ended for property placed in service after December 31, 2025.
